cards.description: Like a filter that removes noisy terminal lines before AI reads them. Directly reduces noisy output from common Git, test, lint and build commands.

cards.shared:
**Runtime:** Install the RTK executable separately in each OS environment. Windows PowerShell:

```powershell
winget install rtk-ai.rtk
```

macOS/Linux with Homebrew:

```bash
brew install rtk
```

Confirm the correct package and capture a baseline:

```terminal
rtk --version
rtk gain
```

**Scope:** The following recipes use user-wide hook setup (`-g`), not project-only setup. Read the dry-run output to identify files and preserve existing hooks. A rules-file fallback asks the model to prefer RTK; it is not the same as automatic command rewriting.
cards.warning: Never replace full logs when details are essential. There is another unrelated `rtk` project: check `rtk gain`.

claude.body:
#### Configure

Preview the user-wide setup:

```terminal
rtk init -g --dry-run
```

Review the named files, then apply:

```terminal
rtk init -g
```

Restart this assistant; inspect its hook manager and complete trust prompts. On Windows confirm your exact RTK release and host support this hook; use the publisher’s WSL or rules fallback if documented for that release.

#### Prove rewriting

Capture `rtk gain`, run one supported repository command through the assistant and inspect the actual command in its tool trace:

```chat
Run git status in this practice repository without editing files. Show the executed command.
```

Run `rtk gain` again. Require both RTK-wrapped command activity and a corresponding new usage entry. If the command was not rewritten, inspect the hook instead of claiming savings.

**Runtime and scope:** Install uv, then the wrapper in this OS environment. The publisher quickstart shows the all-extras Python 3.13 path on macOS Apple Silicon/Linux; on native Windows use its current platform guide and supported wheels/extras rather than treating that path as a tested universal install.

```terminal
uv tool install --python 3.13 "headroom-ai[all]"
```

**Runtime / scope:** Install Node supported by the selected release. The installer registers each chosen assistant separately; installing the runtime does not enable every client.

```terminal
npx claude-mem install
npx claude-mem doctor
npx claude-mem status
```

Select the intended assistant and observer/provider explicitly. Current documentation places memory in `~/.claude-mem`; cloud sync is opt-in. Anonymous usage analytics are enabled by default and can be disabled:

```terminal

```

cards.warning: Never assume perfect memory. Avoid placing company secrets, tokens or private data into unapproved storage.

cards.title: Language Server Plugins
cards.description: Like giving Claude a language-aware dictionary for your code. Higher precision for typed languages.
cards.version: Publisher minimum not established; record installed release before testing.

```chat
/plugin marketplace add anthropics/claude-plugins-official
```



**TypeScript worked example:** Use a TypeScript project with its dependencies installed and an existing `tsconfig.json`. Install the actual language server in this OS environment:

```terminal
npm install -g typescript-language-server typescript
typescript-language-server --version
```

Install `typescript-lsp` below and open an existing `.ts` file. A diagnostic test should use an intentional type mismatch in a disposable fixture; confirm the installed host exposes diagnostics before expecting them. For Python choose `pyright-lsp` and its own prerequisites; one server is not universal.
